Given,

The point $\left(x, y\right)$ satisfies the equation $\dfrac{x + i\left(x - 2\right)}{3 + i} - i = \dfrac{2y + i\left(1 - 3y\right)}{i - 3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x + i\left(x - 2\right)}{\left(3 + i\right)\left(3 - i\right)}\left(3 - i\right) - i = \dfrac{2y + i\left(1 - 3y\right)}{\left(i - 3\right)\left(i + 3\right)}\left(i + 3\right)$

$⇒ \left(x + i\left(x - 2\right)\right)\left(3 - i\right) - 10i = - \left(2y + i\left(1 - 3y\right)\right)\left(i + 3\right)$

$⇒ \left(3x - ix + i\left(x - 2\right)\left(3 - i\right)\right) - 10i = - \left(2iy + 6y + i\left(1 - 3y\right)\left(i + 3\right)\right)$

$⇒ \left(3x - ix + i\left(3x - ix - 6 + 2i\right)\right) - 10i = - \left(2iy + 6y + i\left(i + 3 - 3iy - 9y\right)\right)$

$⇒ \left(3x - ix + 3ix + x - 6i - 2\right) - 10i = - \left(2iy + 6y - 1 + 3i + 3y - 9iy\right)$

$⇒ 4x + 2ix - 13i + 9y - 3 - 7iy = 0$

$⇒ 4x + 9y - 3 + i\left(2x - 13 - 7y\right) = 0$

Now comparing real part and imagenary part we get,

$⇒ 4x + 9y - 3 = 0 . . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$ and $⇒ \left(2x - 13 - 7y\right) = 0 . . . . . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Now solving equation $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$ we get, $x = 3 \text{ and } y = - 1$

Then $x + y = 2$
